question.problem: The point $M$ is the midpoint of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ}.$ What is the value of $x$ if $MQ=x+3$ centimeters and $PM=3x+1$ centimeters?
question.worked_solution:
We have the following diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14171842/assets/4a7ae067ef93ac29b82bbe49571cf389a78b6c0afefda43651044bfe374a733a.png)

Since $M$ is the midpoint of $\overset{―}{PQ}$, the two segments $\overset{―}{PM}$ and $\overset{―}{MQ}$ have the same length. So, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}PM & =MQ \\ 3x+1 & =x+3 \\ 3x+1-x & =x+3-x \\ 2x+1 & =3 \\ 2x+1-1 & =3-1 \\ 2x & =2 \\ \frac{2x}{2} & =\frac{2}{2} \\ x & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=1\,\text{cm}.$
